question:
Water is pumped into a cylindrical tank of radius $2\ \text{m}$ at a constant rate of $0.8\pi\ \text{m}^3/\text{min}$.

(a) Form a relation between the volume $V$ of water and its depth $h$.

(b) Determine the rate at which the water level is rising.

(c) Calculate the time required for the water level to rise from $1.2\ \text{m}$ to $1.7\ \text{m}$.
explanation:
(a)
The volume of water in the cylindrical tank is
$$V=\pi r^2h$$
Since $r=2\ \text{m}$,
$$V=\pi(2)^2h=4\pi h$$

(b)
Differentiating $V=4\pi h$ with respect to time,
$$\frac{dV}{dt}=4\pi\frac{dh}{dt}$$
Given that $\frac{dV}{dt}=0.8\pi\ \text{m}^3/\text{min}$,
$$0.8\pi=4\pi\frac{dh}{dt}$$
Therefore,
$$\frac{dh}{dt}=0.2\ \text{m/min}$$

(c)
The required increase in the water level is
$$1.7-1.2=0.5\ \text{m}$$
Since the water level rises uniformly at $0.2\ \text{m/min}$, the required time is
$$t=\frac{0.5}{0.2}=2.5\ \text{minutes}$$
